proposals.evidence: Perder explicitly analyses taanu milaai as with oneself and illustrates it in example 25: taanu own/self plus milāi with. Both independently attested Dameli bases have reviewed ancestry (tanū-family and milati-family respectively). This is a lexical-constituent analysis of the reflexive phrase, not descent of the whole phrase from a single ancient word.

Perder example 73 explicitly segments my + maternal uncle-OBL + through. Link the lexical constituents to independently attested mā̃ my, mam maternal uncle, and ṣavāi through. The oblique -a is grammatical inflection. This does not add certainty to the deeper ṣavāi analysis: Perder calls its proposed second-causative origin speculative and compares Palula ṣaawaá, while the existing base already has a reviewed link. The present proposal is only the transparent phrase structure.

approval: User: approve all; prefer Pashto where best matched, then Urdu for broadly Perso-Arabic terms. Approval includes qualified analyses, not a claim that uncertainties are resolved.
donor_policy: Prefer an attested Pashto donor where form and meaning fit best; otherwise prefer Urdu for broadly shared Perso-Arabic loans. Preserve explicit source attribution, phonological uncertainty and possible Nuristani mediation. Do not substitute a different dialect merely because its node is linkable.
